rules.statement: A fidei commissum clause prohibiting the lease of property for more than five years is ineffective in the absence of a penalty or forfeiture.
rules.supporting_quote: "No doubt the deed creating the fidei commissum prohibits a lease for a period of more than five years, but, in the absence of a penalty or forfeiture being imposed in the event of a lease exceeding the prescribed limit, the provision is, as Bertram C.J. observed in the case of Saidu v. Samidu [(1922) 23 N. L. R. 506.], ineffective and nothing but a brutum fulmen."
